ce7074c behavioral: wire V-state transport across vsim boundaries
Three coordinated changes that together let RVV C-level fixtures
round-trip v0..v31 through the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 hybrid handoff:

1. apply_resume_from_qemu (simulator.hpp): when the inbound state
   has HYBRID_FLAG_V set, copy state.vreg[] into the fixed scratch
   region of guest RAM via stage_v_to_scratch. The fixture's
   vsim-phase prologue (vle8.v vN, (scratch)) reads it back to
   repopulate the regfile.

2. check_hybrid_handoff (simulator.hpp): when the drain produces a
   state with HYBRID_FLAG_V set, copy scratch RAM bytes back into
   state.vreg[] via read_v_from_scratch before writing the file out.
   This captures any V-reg modifications the fixture made (the
   fixture's epilogue writes vse8.v vN, (scratch) to settle the
   bytes).

3. ResumeDriver (resume_driver.hpp): also restore mtvec via the DM
   Abstract Command path. Otherwise vsim resumes with mtvec=0 and
   any in-vsim trap re-traps at the zero-mapped vector, hanging the
   sim. mstatus / vtype / vl are intentionally NOT restored: vsim's
   DM may not honor abstract-write of mstatus (fixture uses csrs to
   set VS itself), and direct CSR write of vtype sets vill (per V
   spec, vtype must only change via vsetvli).

4. spawn_qemu (qemu_handback.hpp): pass `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`
   to QEMU 2. The default `rv64` CPU has no V extension; mstatus.VS
   is then read-only zero, and the fixture's csrs / vsetvli in
   Phase 3 traps with illegal-instruction. Also ensures Andes
   vendor CSRs (mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl) match QEMU 1.

5. rt_c_v_regs.c: rewritten to do all V work inside the vsim phase
   (Phase A in QEMU 1 only seeds memory). The QEMU plugin's
   gdbstub-pc readback misreports the drain PC when V instructions
   are in flight in QEMU 1 - keeping V purely on the vsim side
   sidesteps that. Phase 3 (in QEMU 2) sets mstatus.VS via csrs
   before vsetvli, since the gdbstub mstatus restore may not carry
   VS through cleanly.
